title: Lending pipeline review
transcript:
Cassandra Hampton: Okay, let's get started, it's one o'clock. Quick agenda: first the open pipeline and anything stuck, then the two files I flagged, then closing calendar for the rest of August. Jasmine, you want to start with credit?
Jasmine Johnson: Sure. Right now I have eleven files in credit review. Most of them are clean. Two are waiting on updated income documentation, and one is sitting on a DTI question that I'd like Lynn's input on. CreditScoring ran fine this morning, so no model delays like we had two weeks ago.
Lynn Chase: Which one is the DTI file?
Jasmine Johnson: It's the refinance for {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0036}}. The existing loan is on {{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00078}}, and the payoff plus the new request pushes the ratio up a bit, though the risk profile is still low. They've been with us since 2020 and the checking on {{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00077}} has had steady deposits the whole time.
Lynn Chase: Right, I know that relationship. I'd say the DTI bump is mostly because the old loan and the new one are both showing in the calculation. Once the payoff is netted, it should come back inside policy. Did you net it?
Jasmine Johnson: Not yet, that's what I wanted to confirm. I wasn't sure whether I could net the payoff before we have the payoff letter.
Brandon George: You can't, not for closing purposes. We need the payoff letter in the file. But for the credit memo you can show a pro forma with the payoff netted and footnote that the letter is pending. That's what we did in June.
Jasmine Johnson: Okay, that works. I'll do the pro forma and footnote it.
Cassandra Hampton: Good. Decision then: Jasmine builds the pro forma memo and sends it to underwriting by end of day Wednesday. Brandon, can you request the payoff letter today?
Brandon George: Yes, I'll request it this afternoon. Usually it takes three to five business days, so we should have it by next Monday at the latest.
Cassandra Hampton: Great. Now, the second file. This is the new checking relationship for {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0049}}, who's applying for a personal loan. Brandi Palmer is the RM, but she's out this week, so Lynn, you're covering?
Lynn Chase: Yes, I'm covering for Brandi through Friday. The client opened checking on {{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00103}} last September. Risk is low. The application is complete except for the employment verification, which is outstanding.
Cassandra Hampton: Has the KYC refresh come through? LoanOrigination pulls from KYCPipeline, and I saw a warning on the file yesterday.
Lynn Chase: I saw that too. I think it's a stale status flag, not a real issue. The KYC was cleared at onboarding. I'll check with the KYC team and ask them to refresh it.
Jasmine Johnson: If it's still flagged tomorrow, let me know. I don't want to start the credit decision on something that might get kicked back.
Lynn Chase: Understood. I'll post in the kyc-pipeline channel this afternoon so it's on record.
Cassandra Hampton: Good. Also, the client asked about a debit card replacement, correct? The card ending on {{CARD_NUMBER:a_00103}}?
Lynn Chase: Yes, they said it was damaged. That's a deposit-side request, not lending, so I'll route it to the client service team rather than handle it ourselves. I'll also confirm the best way to reach them. Their contact preferences are in the CRM under {{CLIENT_EMAIL:c_0049}}, and I'd rather email than call during work hours.
Cassandra Hampton: Perfect. Let's not put any of that in the loan notes, just reference the CRM.
Brandon George: Agreed. On closings, I have four scheduled for this week and six next week. The one risk is the title company delay on the Thursday closing. They've missed two document deadlines already.
Cassandra Hampton: Is it going to slip?
Brandon George: Possibly to Friday. I'll know more tomorrow morning. If it slips, there's no rate lock issue because the lock runs through the end of the month.
Cassandra Hampton: Okay, so that's fine. Please send me an update tomorrow regardless.
Brandon George: Will do. One more thing: for the client {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0036}}, I'd like to call to schedule the signing once the payoff letter lands. Is the number in the file still current?
Jasmine Johnson: Last I checked the CRM listed {{CLIENT_PHONE:c_0036}}, but I'd confirm it, because they updated their email recently.
Brandon George: Got it, I'll confirm before I schedule anything.
Cassandra Hampton: Let's also talk about turnaround time. Our average from application to decision is up to about six business days, and the target is five. Jasmine, is that mostly documentation?
Jasmine Johnson: Mostly, yes. About two-thirds of the delays are waiting on borrowers. I'd suggest a standard document checklist at application, so the RMs can collect everything up front.
Lynn Chase: I like that. I can draft a one-page checklist and circulate it to the relationship managers for comments.
Cassandra Hampton: Great, Lynn, please draft it by Friday. Jasmine, review it for credit requirements before it goes out.
Jasmine Johnson: Happy to.
Cassandra Hampton: Let me recap the action items. Jasmine: pro forma credit memo for the refinance by end of day Wednesday. Brandon: request the payoff letter today, confirm the closing status of the Thursday file tomorrow morning, and verify contact details before scheduling the signing. Lynn: ask KYC to refresh the status flag and post in kyc-pipeline today, route the debit card request to client service, and draft the document checklist by Friday. I'll follow up with underwriting about capacity for next week. Anything else?
Jasmine Johnson: No, that covers it for me.
Brandon George: Nothing from me.
Lynn Chase: All good.
Cassandra Hampton: Thanks, everyone. We'll meet again next Monday at the same time.
